title: Typed variable
code:
const {{name}}: string = "{{text}}";
console.log({{name}});
description: Declare a variable with an explicit type.
explanation: Declare a variable with an explicit type.
usage: Use this when you need to declare a variable with an explicit type.
mistakes: A type annotation uses a colon; it does not validate values at runtime.

title: Number and boolean
description: Use numeric and boolean types.
explanation: Use numeric and boolean types.
usage: Use this when you need to use numeric and boolean types.
mistakes: number includes integer and floating-point values.

title: Typed array
code:
const scores: number[] = [92, 88, 75];
console.log(scores[0]);
description: Restrict array elements to numbers.
explanation: Restrict array elements to numbers.
usage: Use this when you need to restrict array elements to numbers.
mistakes: An out-of-range array access is still possible at runtime.

title: Function
code:
function add(a: number, b: number): number { return a + b; }
console.log(add(2, 3));
description: Type function inputs and return values.
explanation: Type function inputs and return values.
usage: Use this when you need to type function inputs and return values.
mistakes: Return annotations do not change JavaScript runtime semantics.

title: Interface
description: Describe the structure of an object.
explanation: Describe the structure of an object.
usage: Use this when you need to describe the structure of an object.
mistakes: Extra data from a network response still needs runtime validation.

title: Type alias
description: Name a reusable type expression.
explanation: Name a reusable type expression.
usage: Use this when you need to name a reusable type expression.
mistakes: A type alias is a compile-time name, not a runtime constructor.

title: Union narrowing
description: Narrow a union before accessing type-specific methods.
explanation: Narrow a union before accessing type-specific methods.
usage: Use this when you need to narrow a union before accessing type-specific methods.
mistakes: Check typeof before using number-only or string-only methods.

title: Optional property
description: Model a property that may be missing.
explanation: Model a property that may be missing.
usage: Use this when you need to model a property that may be missing.
mistakes: An optional property may be undefined; use a safe fallback.

title: Readonly
description: Prevent a property from being reassigned.
explanation: Prevent a property from being reassigned.
usage: Use this when you need to prevent a property from being reassigned.
mistakes: readonly is a compile-time restriction, not a deep runtime freeze.

title: Tuple
code:
const position: [number, number] = [10, 20];
console.log(position[0]);
description: Store a fixed ordered set of types.
explanation: Store a fixed ordered set of types.
usage: Use this when you need to store a fixed ordered set of types.
mistakes: Tuple positions have distinct meanings and types.

title: Literal union
description: Limit a value to named alternatives.
explanation: Limit a value to named alternatives.
usage: Use this when you need to limit a value to named alternatives.
mistakes: A literal union accepts only its listed alternatives.

title: Typed arrow
code:
const doubleValue = (value: number): number => value * 2;
console.log(doubleValue(3));
description: Create a concise typed function.
explanation: Create a concise typed function.
usage: Use this when you need to create a concise typed function.
mistakes: Keep callback argument and return types consistent.

title: Generic function
code:
function first<T>(items: T[]): T | undefined { return items[0]; }
console.log(first([1, 2, 3]));
description: Preserve a caller’s element type.
explanation: Preserve a caller’s element type.
usage: Use this when you need to preserve a caller’s element type.
mistakes: The first item may be undefined for an empty array.

title: Generic interface
description: Wrap data while preserving its type.
explanation: Wrap data while preserving its type.
usage: Use this when you need to wrap data while preserving its type.
mistakes: Generic parameters preserve type information but add no runtime checks.

title: Record type
code:
const scores: Record<string, number> = { Alex: 92, Sam: 88 };
console.log(scores["Alex"]);
description: Describe a dictionary of consistent values.
explanation: Describe a dictionary of consistent values.
usage: Use this when you need to describe a dictionary of consistent values.
mistakes: A string-keyed Record does not guarantee a requested key exists.

title: Partial type
description: Make all properties optional for an update.
explanation: Make all properties optional for an update.
usage: Use this when you need to make all properties optional for an update.
mistakes: Partial makes every property optional, so validate required fields when merging.

title: Pick type
description: Select only particular properties from a type.
explanation: Select only particular properties from a type.
usage: Use this when you need to select only particular properties from a type.
mistakes: Pick hides fields in the type but does not remove runtime properties.

title: Discriminated union
description: Narrow alternatives using a shared discriminant.
explanation: Narrow alternatives using a shared discriminant.
usage: Use this when you need to narrow alternatives using a shared discriminant.
mistakes: Check the discriminant before reading a variant-specific property.

title: Type guard
description: Validate an unknown value before using it.
explanation: Validate an unknown value before using it.
usage: Use this when you need to validate an unknown value before using it.
mistakes: A type guard must accurately test the runtime value.

title: Async function
code:
async function getName(): Promise<string> { return "Alex"; }
getName().then(console.log).catch(console.error);
description: Declare a typed asynchronous result.
explanation: Declare a typed asynchronous result.
usage: Use this when you need to declare a typed asynchronous result.
mistakes: Await a Promise before treating it as its resolved value.

title: Fetch unknown JSON
description: Fetch JSON without assuming its runtime shape.
explanation: Fetch JSON without assuming its runtime shape.
usage: Use this when you need to fetch JSON without assuming its runtime shape.
mistakes: A Promise<unknown> return makes it clear that the JSON shape is unverified.

title: Error narrowing
code:
try { throw new Error("Invalid input"); }
catch (error: unknown) { console.error(error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)); }
description: Safely inspect a caught unknown error.
explanation: Safely inspect a caught unknown error.
usage: Use this when you need to safely inspect a caught unknown error.
mistakes: Caught errors may be arbitrary values, not just Error objects.

title: Keyof
description: Constrain a key to existing object properties.
explanation: Constrain a key to existing object properties.
usage: Use this when you need to constrain a key to existing object properties.
mistakes: K extends keyof prevents misspelled property names at compile time.

title: Class
description: Define a class with typed state and behavior.
explanation: Define a class with typed state and behavior.
usage: Use this when you need to define a class with typed state and behavior.
mistakes: Access modifiers and types do not replace validation of external input.

title: Module export
code:
export interface Course { name: string; credits: number; }
export const course: Course = { name: "Programming", credits: 3 };
description: Export a type and value from a module.
explanation: Export a type and value from a module.
usage: Use this when you need to export a type and value from a module.
mistakes: Use a module-aware build and import the exported symbols from the generated JavaScript.

title: Satisfies
code:
const settings = { theme: "dark", fontSize: 14 } satisfies { theme: string; fontSize: number };
console.log(settings);
description: Check a value against a type without replacing inference.
explanation: Check a value against a type without replacing inference.
usage: Use this when you need to check a value against a type without replacing inference.
mistakes: satisfies checks compatibility while keeping useful inferred types.

title: Complete typed report
description: Filter and display strongly typed grade records.
explanation: Filter and display strongly typed grade records.
usage: Use this when you need to filter and display strongly typed grade records.
mistakes: Type checking does not guarantee that a server returned valid grade records.
